title: Digital-asset conversion activity layered across on-ramps and wallets
definition: A sequence of conversions between fiat and digital assets across several on-ramps, wallets and counterparties, in which no single step is notable and the sequence as a whole moves value without an apparent commercial purpose. The indicator measures the layering; it does not identify the value's owner or its purpose, and much legitimate activity has the same shape.
evidence_to_cite: the conversion or transaction records, each cited by its own source id and pointer
the account and wallet linkage evidence relied on, and how the linkage was established
the stated business purpose of the digital-asset activity, where one exists
benign_explanations: A customer rebalancing a long-held position across two exchanges for custody reasons.
A merchant accepting digital assets and converting them at several on-ramps to reduce processing fees.
A treasury operation moving funds between an exchange and a cold wallet on a schedule.
A cross-border worker converting remittances at the best available rate.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, guidance on convertible virtual currency and money services businesses, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: Linkage between a fiat account and a wallet is an analytical inference, not a fact. It has to be cited as an inference with its basis stated.
